summary:
We developed Operation Cosmic Daffodil, an interactive 2D space mission design and industrial engineering simulation game created by Team Yalova Daffodils. In this browser-based experience, players act as Chief Mission Logistics Engineers tasked with safely transporting fragile, perishable daffodils from Yalova, Turkey, to deep-space habitats on the Moon and Mars to boost astronaut morale during long-duration missions.

Our project directly addresses the Space Mission Design Game challenge by translating complex aerospace systems engineering and operations research into accessible gameplay. Players solve a multi-constraint 2D cargo-packing problem inside real launch vehicle fairings, balancing payload mass limits, launch budgets, electrical power, Center of Gravity stability, engine bulkhead thermal hazards, and cosmic radiation shielding. Every parameter is grounded in authentic NASA Veggie, Advanced Plant Habitat, BVAD, MSL RAD, and JPL orbital transfer datasets.

This tool is important because real space exploration depends on rigorous resource optimization and engineering trade-offs rather than simply launching rockets. By combining lighthearted storytelling with real NASA telemetry, customizable constraint sliders, and eight dynamic flight failure and success animations, our game makes aerospace logistics and sustainable deep-space life support engaging, intuitive, and educational for students, engineers, and space enthusiasts everywhere.
details:
What It Does & How It Works Operation Cosmic Daffodil is an interactive 2D space mission design and aerospace logistics simulation game developed by Team Yalova Daffodils. Players take on the role of Chief Mission Logistics Engineer tasked with transporting fragile, perishable daffodils from Yalova, Turkey, to deep-space habitats in Low Earth Orbit, the Moon, and Mars to support astronaut psychological well-being during long-duration missions.

The gameplay unfolds across three integrated stages: • Trajectory & Launch Vehicle Selection: Players choose a destination and transfer profile (ISS LEO, Lunar Artemis, Mars Hohmann Transfer, or Mars Fast Trajectory) and pair it with real-world rockets (Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy, Vulcan Centaur, Starship, or NASA SLS), balancing transit duration against delta-v payload penalties and launch costs. • 2D Fairing Cargo Optimization (5x4 Matrix): Inside the rocket payload fairing, players arrange Daffodil Biopods, Cryo-HVAC cooling units, Lead Radiation Shields, Solar/RTG Power Modules, and Structural Counterweights while monitoring live telemetry gauges for mass, budget, electrical power, thermal risk, radiation attenuation, and Center of Gravity (CoG) stability. • Real-Time Flight Simulation Theater: Once configured, players launch the mission in a NASA TV-style live telemetry theater featuring an internal fairing picture-in-picture camera and eight distinct animated outcomes—including liftoff thermal bulkhead fires, aerodynamic CoG tumble breakups, deep-space freezing, cosmic-ray mutations, NASA OIG budget cancellations, or successful planetary arrival.

Benefits & Intended Impact Real spaceflight is governed by strict resource constraints and engineering trade-offs rather than simply building larger rockets. By translating complex aerospace systems engineering and industrial engineering concepts—such as the 2D Knapsack packing problem, perishable cold-chain logistics, and lead-time optimization—into visual, hands-on gameplay, the project makes orbital mechanics and sustainable life-support design intuitive for students, educators, and space enthusiasts. Users can also toggle between strict NASA baseline limits and custom manual mass/budget sliders to run their own engineering sensitivity experiments.

Tools, Languages, Software & Data Used • Languages & Web Technologies: HTML5 Canvas API (2D flight rendering, particle physics, and telemetry HUD), Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+ physics and constraint engine), CSS3 / Tailwind CSS (mission-control dashboard UI), and the Web Audio API (synthesized cockpit Master Caution voice and tone alerts). • Development & Hosting Environment: Developed on standard personal computers without specialized hardware requirements and deployed as a zero-dependency, single-file web application hosted via Google Sites for instant browser accessibility across desktop and mobile devices. • NASA Open Data Integration: Calibrated using NASA Veggie and Advanced Plant Habitat (APH) growth parameters, NASA Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD) ECLSS metrics, Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Radiation Assessment Detector (RAD) cosmic-ray dosage rates, and NASA/JPL launch vehicle and trajectory specifications.

Creativity & Key Engineering Factors Considered Rather than relying on generic sci-fi combat or abstract menus, our team blended a culturally rooted, human-centric story—bringing living daffodils from Yalova to boost astronaut morale—with authentic engineering failure physics. Key factors our team modeled include: • Thermal Bulkhead Proximity: Placing flammable biopods in the bottom row adjacent to the hot engine bulkhead without active cooling triggers a cockpit Master Caution warning and causes a blazing liftoff failure. • Aerodynamic Center of Gravity (CoG): Asymmetric cargo placement shifts the lateral CoG vector beyond safe aerodynamic tolerances during Max-Q. • Lead-Time vs. Delta-V Trade-Offs: Slower Hohmann transfers carry heavier payloads cheaply but expose biological cargo to prolonged cosmic radiation and thermal decay, whereas fast trajectories demand high-capacity rockets and strict mass discipline. • Accessibility & Performance: Designed to load instantaneously in any modern web browser with zero installation barriers.
